events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Rio Puerco Near Bernardo affecting Socorro County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Puerco near Bernardo.

* WHEN...Until Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, Streets in the village of San Francisco
between interstate 25 and the Rio Grande just south of Bernardo
will flood. Water levels in the Lower Rio Puerco have not been this
high since July of 1944. The nearby railroad bridge may flood.
Further rises would impact Interstate 25 traffic.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:00 PM MDT Sunday the stage was 17.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage this afternoon
to 24.1 feet just after midnight tonight. It will then fall early
Tuesday afternoon. It will rise again to 22.5 feet Wednesday
morning. It will then fall below flood stage early Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 19.5 feet.
- Flood History...No available flood history.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Northwestern Valencia County in central New Mexico...
Northeastern Cibola County in west central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 330 PM MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 226 PM MDT, emergency management reported continued flooding
through the Rio San Jose basin, which is still out of banks in
large stretches. Any additional rainfall this afternoon will
exacerbate ongoing flooding.
- Flooding will continue along the Rio San Jose.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Grants, Laguna Pueblo, New Laguna, Cubero, Mesita, San Fidel,
Skyline-Ganipa, McCartys, Paraje and Seama.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding along the Little Colorado River from earlier
excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Birdsprings to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until 900 AM MST /1000 AM MDT/ Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring near
Birdsprings. Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 111 PM MST /211 PM MDT/, water levels have fallen below action
stage at Winslow and will continue to fall this afternoon.
However, downstream impacts will continue near Birdsprings
through Monday morning.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 1:00pm MST /2:00pm MDT/ the stage was 16.94 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Water levels have fallen below action stage and will
continue to fall through this afternoon.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Birdsprings will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow.

- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 327 PM CDT/227 PM MDT/, Doppler radar was tracking a strong
thunderstorm 22 miles southeast of McKittrick Canyon, or 24 miles
east of Pine Springs, moving northeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

This storm will remain over mainly rural areas of southern Eddy and
northeastern Culberson Counties.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Catastrophic flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected along the San Juan River between Four Corners and Mexican
Hat. This is an emergency situation!

* WHERE...Western Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 600 AM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along San Juan River is occurring or expected to
begin shortly. The crest will occur around Aneth, Montezuma Creek
and Bluff this afternoon and evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 204 PM MDT, Sunday the stage for the San Juan river near Bluff
was 20 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon to a crest of 29.5 feet early Monday morning. It will
then fall below flood stage early Tuesday morning.
- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 32.0
feet on 09/10/1927.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Tselakai Dezza, Bluff, Halchita, Montezuma Creek and
Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...West Central Chaves County in southeastern New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 500 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos.
Dangerous flows over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 203 PM MDT, trained weather spotters reported high flows over
low water crossings in the Rio Felix downstream to Dexter caused
by earlier rainfall. This is causing arroyo and small stream
flooding.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Whitetail Canyon, Made Well, Walnut Creek, Eagle Creek, Indian
Canyon, Monument Canyon, Lincoln Canyon, Felix, Rio and Pecos
River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of West Central Chaves County.
